name: Elioenai
overview: Elioenai was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Becher. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional personal details or notable events recorded beyond his lineage. This brief record situates him within the genealogical framework of Israel's tribes.
namesAndTitles: The name Elioenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional focus on the Lord. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:8, conveys a personal orientation toward God, although it was not explicitly given by God Himself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elioenai as the son of Becher, anchoring his identity within the Benjaminite family line. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented for Elioenai.
scriptureSignificance: Elioenai's significance lies in his role within the genealogical records that preserve the heritage of the tribe of Benjamin. As the son of Becher, his inclusion in 1 Chronicles 7:8 contributes to the biblical record of Israel's tribal lineage, which undergirds God's providential plan for His people. Though the narrative does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his mention affirms the continuity of God's covenant community through successive generations.
